2026-186.headline: Portland Creates Psychedelic Health and Safety Rules
2026-186.summary: Portland established a new city code governing psychedelic health and safety. The regulations set local guidelines and safety standards for the use and administration of psychedelic substances. These rules apply to service providers, businesses, and residents participating in regulated psychedelic programs within the city.
2026-186.title: Add Psychedelic Health and Safety Code (add Code Chapter 14B.140)

2026-223.headline: City Adopts FY 2026-27 Supplemental Budget
2026-223.summary: Portland updated its 2026-27 budget to adjust city spending and manage financial risks to municipal services. The changes reallocate funds across city departments to help maintain existing public programs and services.
2026-223.title: Adopt a Supplemental Budget for FY 2026-27 to reduce potential risks to City services

2026-236.headline: Portland Leases Eastside Office for Safety Division
2026-236.summary: Portland's Community Safety Division is securing a new eastside office through a five-year lease with American Property Management. The agreement provides space for staff who coordinate local safety and emergency response programs. The move affects eastside residents accessing division services and city staff working in the area.
2026-236.title: *Authorize a five-year lease with American Property Management for Community Safety Division eastside office

2026-248.headline: City Begins Foreclosure on NE Sandy Property
2026-248.summary: The City of Portland is starting foreclosure proceedings on a property located at 7545 NE Sandy Boulevard to collect unpaid city liens. This process allows the city to recover unpaid debt owed by the property owner. If the debt remains unpaid, the property may be sold through a court process.
2026-248.title: Initiate foreclosure action on 7545 WI/NE Sandy Blvd for the collection of delinquent City Liens placed against the property

2026-250.headline: City Begins Foreclosure on N Columbia Blvd Property
2026-250.summary: Portland is initiating foreclosure on a North Columbia Boulevard property to collect unpaid city liens. The action allows the city to claim or sell the site to recover unpaid debts. It directly impacts the property owner while enforcing local debt collection policies.
2026-250.title: Initiate foreclosure action on N Columbia Blvd for the collection of delinquent City Liens placed against the property

2026-267.headline: City Pays $287,500 Settlement for Water Bureau Crash
2026-267.summary: The City of Portland will pay $287,500 to settle a lawsuit over a collision involving a Portland Water Bureau dump truck. The payment resolves claims made by an individual for bodily injuries suffered in the crash.
2026-267.title: *Pay settlement of Michael Duffer bodily injury lawsuit in the sum of $287,500 resulting from a collision with a City dump truck involving the Portland Water Bureau

2026-277.headline: City accepts $207K grant to curb street racing
2026-277.summary: Portland is accepting $207,411 in grant funding to address illegal street racing and street takeovers. The money will support targeted law enforcement patrols and enforcement efforts across the city. This affects drivers and residents living in neighborhoods impacted by street takeovers.
2026-277.title: *Appropriate grant award of $207,411 for speed racing street takeover

2026-278.headline: City Accepts $103,069 Grant for Traffic Enforcement
2026-278.summary: Portland will use a $103,069 grant to increase traffic enforcement patrols across the city. The funds will pay for officer overtime focused on traffic safety and law enforcement. This change affects drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians traveling on local streets.
2026-278.title: *Appropriate grant award of $103,069 for expanded traffic enforcement

2026-280.headline: City approves terms for Moda Center arena renovation
2026-280.summary: A new non-binding framework sets initial terms for major renovations at the Moda Center arena. The agreement aims to keep the Portland Trail Blazers playing in the city for at least another 20 years. It establishes guidelines for future operating and lease contracts between the city and team management.
2026-280.title: Authorize a non-binding term sheet with Rip City Management LLC and Trail Blazers Holdings, LLC outlining the terms for Moda Center arena renovation, operating and lease agreements that will keep the Portland Trail Blazers playing in Portland for at least 20 more years

2026-285.headline: City Seeks Partner to Develop Moda Center Land
2026-285.summary: Portland is beginning a search for a partner to build on city-owned land near the Moda Center. The city administrator will create a process to select a developer for these Rose Quarter properties. This move sets the stage for future construction and revitalization around the arena.
2026-285.title: Direct the City Administrator to advance a process to identify a development partner for City-owned properties adjacent to the Moda Center

2026-294.headline: City to Subsidize Transit Passes for Employees
2026-294.summary: A new pilot program will subsidize public transit passes for Portland city employees. Funding for the program comes from an increase of up to $245,000 in city bureau rates for the 2026-27 fiscal year. The decision affects municipal workers and city bureau budgets.
2026-294.title: *Authorize an increase up to $245,000 in bureau rates for FY 2026-27 to implement a pilot program to subsidize transit passes for City employees

2026-339.headline: City Settles Bicycle Crash Lawsuit for $125,000
2026-339.summary: The City of Portland will pay $125,000 to settle a lawsuit with a cyclist injured in a crash involving the Portland Bureau of Transportation. The payment covers bodily injuries sustained by Joseph Rios during the incident. This agreement resolves all legal claims against the city related to the crash.
2026-339.title: *Pay settlement of Joseph Rios bodily injury lawsuit in the sum of $125,000 resulting from a bicycle crash involving Portland Bureau of Transportation
